clue.text: Spy a curly hair on the rug

parts.note: a rug or floor mat is a small floor covering
taken as written

indicators.note: curly hair is twisted out of line, so the letters of these words are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices a curled strand of hair lying on the carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curly' is the anagram signal on 'a hair'; 'on the' only links. Mata Hari was the Dutch dancer shot as a German spy in 1917.
explanation.definitionFit: Mata Hari is history's most famous female secret agent, so her name stands for a spy.

clue.text: When to tell all?

parts.note: tell here is the old sense of count, as a bank teller counts: the occasion for counting every person in the land

explanation.surface: A question about the right moment to make a full confession.
explanation.definitionFit: An official population count is when a state numbers, or tells, all its people.

clue.text: Peel read out what he did to the Corn Laws

definitions.text: what he did to the Corn Laws

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A history lesson in which the speaker reads out Robert Peel's achievement on the Corn Laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'read out' but signals an anagram of PEEL READ. Sir Robert Peel, British prime minister, scrapped the Corn Laws, tariffs on imported grain, in 1846.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel abolished the grain tariffs by Act of Parliament, which is to revoke or annul them.

clue.text: Some solace in failed investment

definitions.meaning: a measure of comfort or easing of distress
investment is the military besieging of a town; when the siege is broken, the town is freed by its rescuers

explanation.surface: Losing money on a bad deal brings at least a little comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' looks financial but is the old word for a siege; the arrival of a force that lifts a siege is its relief, as at Mafeking. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief means both comfort after distress and the lifting of a siege by a rescuing force.

clue.text: Gathered in study to hold exercises

indicators.note: one word holds the other, so the exercises go inside the study word

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Collected during a study session that included some workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap a harvest is to cut and gather it in, so reaped is a synonym of gathered in.

clue.text: Confirm a try, if converted properly

indicators.note: in rugby a converted try is followed by a kick; here the letters are converted into another word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby referee awards a try provided the conversion kick is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted properly' looks like rugby, where a try is converted by a kick at goal; it rearranges A TRY IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify an agreement is to approve or validate it formally.

clue.text: Latest schism besetting church

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so the schism word goes round the church

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear, as in a rift in a group
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The newest split to trouble the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent means most lately happened, a synonym of latest.

clue.text: Inclined to be guarded

definitions.meaning: ... as in leaned towards, had a tendency
... as in looked after, watched over

explanation.definitionFit: Tended is the past of both tend (to lean towards) and tend (to look after).

clue.text: Man using mashie and spoon going round

indicators.note: going round suggests letters circling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; a mashie is an old golf club
taken as written; a spoon is an old lofted golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer playing a round with old-fashioned clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' looks like a round of golf but is the anagram signal; 'and' joins the fodder and 'using' links. Both fodder words are old names for golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is the scientific name of the human species, mankind in general.

clue.text: Doesn't go right inside, but wanders around

indicators.note: inside places the right letter within the word for not going

parts.note: to stay is to remain rather than leave

explanation.surface: Someone who won't go in properly but roams about instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to roam or wander from the proper path.

clue.text: Debit one transferred, following orders

indicators.note: transferred, an accounting word here, moves the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An accounts clerk dutifully moves a debit entry as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transferred' sounds like book-keeping but rearranges DEBIT ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient person does as told, which is following orders.

clue.text: A bad start for an ancient king

parts.note: food gone off has turned bad

indicators.note: the start for a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An old monarch who got off on the wrong foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start for' takes the A of 'an'; the opening 'A' only links. Offa was the 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, so he is an ancient English king.

clue.text: Robber holding up store?

parts.note: a store robbed at gunpoint is held up, but read literally the thief is one who lifts things from a shop

explanation.surface: An armed robber raiding a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who takes goods from shops is literally someone who lifts from a store.

clue.text: Shooting stick?

parts.note: a shooting stick is a spiked walking stick with a fold-out seat; here it is a stick used for shooting balls on a green baize table

explanation.surface: A folding seat-stick of the kind used at country events.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting stick is a British walking stick that opens into a seat, used at race meetings; the answer is a stick for potting shots on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiard players strike, or shoot, the balls with a long tapered stick.

clue.text: Left to old seamen in Labrador resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort: the letters are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Retired sailors abandoned at a holiday spot in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but means re-sort LABRADOR; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard was the old naval term for the left-hand side of a ship, later replaced by port.

clue.text: Mounting disorder

definitions.meaning: a revolt or rebellion, civil unrest

explanation.surface: Unrest in the streets is getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is both a rising up and a popular rebellion against authority.

clue.text: Metal grating to cook eggs initially

parts.note: to grill is to cook under direct heat

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A metal rack on which eggs are cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grid of metal bars over an opening, a grating.

clue.text: Compass cover

definitions.meaning: extent or range, as in the compass of a voice

explanation.definitionFit: Spread means range or extent, and is also a covering such as a bedspread.

clue.text: Parking, reversing badly, generating a jam

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: done badly, the letters come out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A clumsy driver reversing into a parking space causes a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is the anagram signal on 'reversing'. The jam is fruit preserve, not a traffic jam caused by bad parking.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserving fruit by boiling it with sugar is how jam is made.

clue.text: It's a sound move — that's plain

indicators.note: sound tells the solver the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a step is a move made with the foot

explanation.surface: A remark that a sensible move is a straightforward one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like sensible but signals a homophone: STEP sounds like STEPPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland of eastern Europe and Asia, a type of plain.

clue.text: Cracked jokes when bound not to speak

definitions.meaning: to gag is to tell jokes, as a comedian's gags
having a gag tied over the mouth to silence someone

explanation.surface: A comedian who kept joking until he was gagged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gagged means both made jokes, or gags, and silenced with a cloth bound over the mouth.

clue.text: Utterly absorbed in something, say

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken aloud

parts.note: to be in a wrapping or covering is to be wrapped

explanation.surface: Completely engrossed in a particular activity, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but signals a homophone: WRAPPED, meaning inside something, is said like RAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt describes total engrossment, fully absorbed in attention.

clue.text: Once in a lifetime phenomenon?

parts.note: the idiom for something very rare, literally a second full moon in a calendar month

explanation.surface: Something rare that happens only once in a person's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom once in a blue moon means very rarely, from the uncommon second full moon in a month.

clue.text: A sort of music providing the message

definitions.meaning: a style of American Christian music with roots in Black churches
the Christian message, the good news of the four Evangelists

explanation.surface: Music that carries a moral message.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel is a genre of church music and also the Christian message, literally good news.

clue.text: Former forward, one who should know better

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
pert means cheeky, forward in manner

explanation.surface: A cheeky ex-partner who ought to have behaved better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should know better' is read literally: an authority knows more than others.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a specialist who knows a subject better than most people.

clue.text: Drink for each returning academic

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

indicators.note: returning means the academic word is read backwards

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A round of drinks for each lecturer coming back to college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DON into NOD. Pernod is a French aniseed aperitif.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a brand of aniseed-flavoured French spirit, a type of drink.
